passages.text: Hear now what the LORD says: “Arise, plead your case before the mountains, and let the hills hear your voice.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is speaking.
The LORD gives a command.
Listen to what the LORD says.
Stand up now.
Present your case before the mountains.
Let the hills hear your voice.
passages.original: שִׁמְעוּ־ נָ֕א אֵ֥ת אֲשֶׁר־ יְהוָ֖ה אֹמֵ֑ר ק֚וּם רִ֣יב אֶת־ הֶהָרִ֔ים וְתִשְׁמַ֥עְנָה הַגְּבָע֖וֹת קוֹלֶֽךָ׃

passages.text: Hear, O mountains, the LORD’s indictment, you enduring foundations of the earth. For the LORD has a case against His people, and He will argue it against Israel: ‘My people, what have I done to you? Testify against Me how I have wearied you!
passages.sermon:
The LORD is speaking.
The LORD is holy and just.
The LORD calls the mountains to listen.
The LORD calls the strong foundations of the earth to listen.
The LORD has a complaint against His people.
The LORD will argue His case against Israel.
The LORD says, “My people, what have I done to you?”
The LORD asks, “How have I made you tired?”
The LORD commands, “Answer Me.”
passages.original: שִׁמְע֤וּ הָרִים֙ אֶת־ רִ֣יב יְהוָ֔ה וְהָאֵתָנִ֖ים מֹ֣סְדֵי אָ֑רֶץ כִּ֣י רִ֤יב לַֽיהוָה֙ עִם־ עַמּ֔וֹ וְעִם־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל יִתְוַכָּֽח׃ עַמִּ֛י מֶה־ עָשִׂ֥יתִי לְךָ֖ וּמָ֣ה הֶלְאֵתִ֑יךָ עֲנֵ֥ה בִּֽי׃

passages.text: For I brought you up from the land of Egypt and redeemed you from the house of slavery. I sent Moses before you, as well as Aaron and Miriam.
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks to His people Israel.
The LORD brought Israel up from the land of Egypt.
The LORD redeemed Israel from the house of slavery.
The LORD sent Moses before Israel.
The LORD also sent Aaron before Israel.
The LORD also sent Miriam before Israel.
passages.original: כִּ֤י הֶעֱלִתִ֙יךָ֙ מֵאֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרַ֔יִם וּמִבֵּ֥ית עֲבָדִ֖ים פְּדִיתִ֑יךָ וָאֶשְׁלַ֣ח לְפָנֶ֔יךָ אֶת־ מֹשֶׁ֖ה אַהֲרֹ֥ן וּמִרְיָֽם׃

passages.text: My people, remember what Balak king of Moab counseled and what Balaam son of Beor answered. Remember your journey from Shittim to Gilgal, so that you may acknowledge the righteousness of the LORD.’ ”
passages.sermon:
God speaks to His people Israel.
God calls them "My people."
God tells them to remember important events.
Balak was the king of Moab.
Balak gave advice against Israel.
Balaam was the son of Beor.
Balaam answered Balak.
God tells His people to remember what Balak planned.
God tells them to remember what Balaam replied.
God tells His people to remember their journey.
They traveled from Shittim to Gilgal.
God wants His people to remember these things.
God wants them to know His righteousness.
passages.original: עַמִּ֗י זְכָר־ נָא֙ מַה־ יָּעַ֗ץ בָּלָק֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ מוֹאָ֔ב וּמֶה־ עָנָ֥ה אֹת֖וֹ בִּלְעָ֣ם בֶּן־ בְּע֑וֹר מִן־ הַשִּׁטִּים֙ עַד־ הַגִּלְגָּ֔ל לְמַ֕עַן דַּ֖עַת צִדְק֥וֹת יְהוָֽה׃

passages.text: With what shall I come before the LORD when I bow before the God on high? Should I come to Him with burnt offerings, with year-old calves?
passages.sermon:
I want to approach the LORD.
The LORD is the God on high.
I want to bow before Him.
I ask what I should bring to Him.
Should I come with burnt offerings?
Should I bring year-old calves?
passages.original: בַּמָּה֙ אֲקַדֵּ֣ם יְהוָ֔ה אִכַּ֖ף לֵאלֹהֵ֣י מָר֑וֹם הַאֲקַדְּמֶ֣נּוּ בְעוֹל֔וֹת בַּעֲגָלִ֖ים בְּנֵ֥י שָׁנָֽה׃

passages.text: Would the LORD be pleased with thousands of rams, with ten thousand rivers of oil? Shall I present my firstborn for my transgression, the fruit of my body for the sin of my soul?
passages.sermon:
The LORD is God.
The LORD is holy.
Would the LORD be pleased with thousands of rams?
Would the LORD be pleased with ten thousand rivers of oil?
Should I give my firstborn for my transgression?
Should I give the fruit of my body for the sin of my soul?
passages.original: הֲיִרְצֶ֤ה יְהוָה֙ בְּאַלְפֵ֣י אֵילִ֔ים בְּרִֽבְב֖וֹת נַֽחֲלֵי־ שָׁ֑מֶן הַאֶתֵּ֤ן בְּכוֹרִי֙ פִּשְׁעִ֔י פְּרִ֥י בִטְנִ֖י חַטַּ֥את נַפְשִֽׁי׃

passages.text: He has shown you, O man, what is good. And what does the LORD require of you but to act justly, to love mercy, and to walk humbly with your God?
passages.sermon:
God speaks to every person.
God shows you what is good.
God tells you what He wants from you.
God does not want empty sacrifices.
God wants you to act justly.
God wants you to love mercy.
God wants you to walk humbly with Him.
God is your God.
God requires justice, mercy, and humility.
passages.original: הִגִּ֥יד לְךָ֛ אָדָ֖ם מַה־ טּ֑וֹב וּמָֽה־ יְהוָ֞ה דּוֹרֵ֣שׁ מִמְּךָ֗ כִּ֣י אִם־ עֲשׂ֤וֹת מִשְׁפָּט֙ וְאַ֣הֲבַת חֶ֔סֶד וְהַצְנֵ֥עַ לֶ֖כֶת עִם־ אֱלֹהֶֽיךָ׃פ

passages.text: The voice of the LORD calls out to the city (and it is sound wisdom to fear Your name): “Heed the rod and the One who ordained it.
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks with authority.
The LORD calls out to the city.
The LORD’s voice is clear.
It is wise to fear the LORD’s name.
Listen to the rod.
Pay attention to the one who appointed the rod.
The LORD commands respect and obedience.
passages.original: ק֤וֹל יְהוָה֙ לָעִ֣יר יִקְרָ֔א וְתוּשִׁיָּ֖ה יִרְאֶ֣ה שְׁמֶ֑ךָ שִׁמְע֥וּ מַטֶּ֖ה וּמִ֥י יְעָדָֽהּ׃

passages.text: Can I forget any longer, O house of the wicked, the treasures of wickedness and the short ephah, which is accursed?
passages.sermon:
God speaks to the house of the wicked.
The house of the wicked stores treasures gained by evil.
The house of the wicked uses a short ephah.
A short ephah is a dishonest measure.
A short ephah is cursed.
God asks if He can forget these things any longer.
passages.original: ע֗וֹד הַאִשׁ֙ בֵּ֣ית רָשָׁ֔ע אֹצְר֖וֹת רֶ֑שַׁע וְאֵיפַ֥ת רָז֖וֹן זְעוּמָֽה׃

passages.text: Can I excuse dishonest scales or bags of false weights?
passages.sermon:
God speaks to the people.
God asks a question.
God says, "Can I excuse dishonest scales?"
God says, "Can I excuse bags that hold false weights?"
passages.original: הַאֶזְכֶּ֖ה בְּמֹ֣אזְנֵי רֶ֑שַׁע וּבְכִ֖יס אַבְנֵ֥י מִרְמָֽה׃

passages.text: For the wealthy of the city are full of violence, and its residents speak lies; their tongues are deceitful in their mouths.
passages.sermon:
The wealthy people in the city act with violence.
The residents of the city speak lies.
Their tongues speak deceit.
They use their mouths to deceive.
passages.original: אֲשֶׁ֤ר עֲשִׁירֶ֙יהָ֙ מָלְא֣וּ חָמָ֔ס וְיֹשְׁבֶ֖יהָ דִּבְּרוּ־ שָׁ֑קֶר וּלְשׁוֹנָ֖ם רְמִיָּ֥ה בְּפִיהֶֽם׃

passages.text: Therefore I am striking you severely, to ruin you because of your sins.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to the people.
God says, “I am striking you.”
I strike you with sickness.
I do this to destroy you.
I do this because of your sins.
passages.original: וְגַם־ אֲנִ֖י הֶחֱלֵ֣יתִי הַכּוֹתֶ֑ךָ הַשְׁמֵ֖ם עַל־ חַטֹּאתֶֽךָ׃

passages.text: You will eat but not be satisfied, and your hunger will remain with you. What you acquire, you will not preserve; and what you save, I will give to the sword.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to the sinful people of the city.
You will eat food.
You will not be satisfied.
Hunger will stay inside you.
You will try to save what you have.
You will not keep it safe.
What you manage to save, I will give to the sword.
You will lose it in violence and war.
passages.original: אַתָּ֤ה תֹאכַל֙ וְלֹ֣א תִשְׂבָּ֔ע וְיֶשְׁחֲךָ֖ בְּקִרְבֶּ֑ךָ וְתַסֵּג֙ וְלֹ֣א תַפְלִ֔יט וַאֲשֶׁ֥ר תְּפַלֵּ֖ט לַחֶ֥רֶב אֶתֵּֽן׃

passages.text: You will sow but not reap; you will press olives but not anoint yourselves with oil; you will tread grapes but not drink the wine.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to the people of Israel.
God warns them because of their sins.
You will plant seeds in the ground.
You will not gather any harvest.
You will press olives to get oil.
You will not use the oil to anoint yourselves.
You will crush grapes to make wine.
You will not drink the wine.
passages.original: אַתָּ֥ה תִזְרַ֖ע וְלֹ֣א תִקְצ֑וֹר אַתָּ֤ה תִדְרֹֽךְ־ זַ֙יִת֙ וְלֹא־ תָס֣וּךְ שֶׁ֔מֶן וְתִיר֖וֹשׁ וְלֹ֥א תִשְׁתֶּה־ יָּֽיִן׃

passages.text: You have kept the statutes of Omri and all the practices of Ahab’s house; you have followed their counsel. Therefore I will make you a desolation, and your inhabitants an object of contempt; you will bear the scorn of the nations.”
passages.sermon:
The people of Israel have followed the statutes of Omri.
They have done all the practices of Ahab’s house.
They have listened to the advice of these wicked rulers.
Because of this, I will make you a desolation.
Your land will become empty and ruined.
Your people will become an object of contempt.
Other nations will mock you.
You will carry the shame of my people.
passages.original: וְיִשְׁתַּמֵּ֞ר חֻקּ֣וֹת עָמְרִ֗י וְכֹל֙ מַעֲשֵׂ֣ה בֵית־ אַחְאָ֔ב וַתֵּלְכ֖וּ בְּמֹֽעֲצוֹתָ֑ם לְמַעַן֩ תִּתִּ֨י אֹתְךָ֜ לְשַׁמָּ֗ה וְיֹשְׁבֶ֙יהָ֙ לִשְׁרֵקָ֔ה וְחֶרְפַּ֥ת עַמִּ֖י תִּשָּֽׂאוּ׃פ
